Simulate a metacommunity

Source: R/dynamics.R
simulate_metacommunity.Rd

Runs the process-based model of Thompson et al. (2020) on a landscape. At each time step, abundances are drawn as \(N' \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(r N / (1 + N \alpha'))\), where \(r\) holds the growth rates of each species at each site (growth_rates()) and \(\alpha\) the competition coefficients (competition_matrix()). Each individual then emigrates with probability dispersal, and emigrants are redistributed among sites:

Usage

simulate_metacommunity(
  landscape,
  traits,
  alpha,
  dispersal = 0.01,
  n_steps = 1000,
  env_time = NULL,
  seed_steps = seq(10, 100, 10),
  seed_mean = 0.5,
  record_steps = NULL,
  extirpation = 0,
  pool = NULL,
  initial = NULL,
  immigration = c("poisson", "multinomial"),
  env = NULL,
  evolution = NULL,
  disturbance = 0
)

Arguments

landscape

An mc_landscape object.

traits

Species traits from species_traits(), or, for a niche with several environmental axes, a list of them, one per column of env, with the same species; see growth_rates().

alpha

Competition matrix from competition_matrix(). Species are matched to the rows of traits by name, or by position if alpha has no names.

dispersal

Emigration probability, one value or one per species.

n_steps

Number of time steps.

env_time

Optional matrix (sites x n_steps) with the environment at each step, e.g. from env_over_time(). If NULL, the environment of the landscape is constant. With env (several axes), a list with one such matrix per column of env (matched by name when named), or an array of sites x steps x axes.

seed_steps

Steps at which individuals are added during colonisation.

seed_mean

Mean number of individuals of each species added to each site at each seeding step (and at the start).

record_steps

Optional steps at which abundances are recorded.

extirpation

Probability that a population is lost at each time step, one value or one per species.

pool

Optional matrix (sites x species), logical or 0/1, with the sites where each species can occur.

initial

Optional matrix (sites x species) of abundances or 0/1 presences at the start, only where pool allows.

immigration

How emigrants reach other sites on spatially explicit landscapes: "poisson" (the default, as in the code of Thompson et al. 2020) or "multinomial", which conserves them. Spatially implicit landscapes are always multinomial.

env

Optional environmental axes of each site, a matrix or data frame with one row per site and one column per element of traits (such as the env of several landscapes on the same grid). Needed when traits is a list; replaces the env of landscape. With env_time, it gives the axes (names and number), and the environment of each step comes from env_time. Columns without names take the names of traits, or axis1, axis2, ...

evolution

Optional settings from evolution_control() for the evolution of the niche optimum within each population: selection by the local environment, drift, gene flow, founder sampling and plasticity. NULL (the default) keeps the optimum of each species in all its populations, as before. With a niche of several axes, one trait evolves per axis, with covariance matrices \(G\) and \(E\) (see the section Several traits of evolution_control() and genetic_matrices()).

disturbance

Probability that a site loses all its populations at each time step (one value; 0, the default, for none).

Value

An mc_sim object: a list with abundance (sites x species matrix at the last step), history (sites x species x recorded steps array, or NULL), and the landscape, traits, alpha, dispersal, extirpation and pool used, env when given, and tree when the traits came from species_traits() with a tree, the colonisation history (arrival, propagule, immigrants, migrant_load; see the section Colonisation history) and n_steps. With evolution, also evolution, a list with the genetic mean of the optimum in each population (genetic), the plastic part of its phenotype at the last step (plastic), the phenotype after dispersal (phenotype, which mixes residents and immigrants), the genetic means and the environment at record_steps (history, environment_history), the reference environment and the settings, and, with mutation_var, the genetic variance of each population at the last step (genetic_variance); NA where a population is absent. With several evolving traits, genetic, plastic and phenotype are arrays of sites x species x traits, history has the recorded steps as a fourth dimension, and genetic_var, env_var (one matrix per species) and plasticity (species x traits) are kept. With a niche of several axes, as_mc_data() keeps every axis (env and one optimum_ column of traits per axis), while summary_stats() uses the first axis unless given trait and env, and sample_individuals() needs a single axis unless the traits evolved (source = "evolution", one column per trait).

Details

  • spatially implicit landscapes (landscape_implicit()): the emigrants of each species are distributed multinomially, each site receiving them with probability proportional to the number of emigrants from the other sites (a uniform kernel; an individual may return to its own site);

  • spatially explicit landscapes (landscape_grid()): the number of immigrants of each species at each site is drawn from a Poisson distribution whose mean is the expected flow of emigrants through the dispersal kernel. This approximation does not conserve the number of dispersing individuals exactly, but has the right expectation. The code of Thompson et al. (2020) does the same. Few emigrants may then produce no immigrant, so with extirpation and low dispersal, recolonisation is rarer than in mcomsimr, which conserves dispersers. With immigration = "multinomial", the emigrants of each species at each site are instead distributed among the other sites multinomially, with the probabilities of the kernel, which conserves them. It costs about as much as the Poisson draw at low dispersal and up to 20 times more at high dispersal, where the two give nearly the same results.

After dispersal, each population is lost with probability extirpation, independently of its size. Thompson et al. (2020) used 0.002 in their competition-colonisation scenario and no extirpation in the others. With disturbance, each site then loses all its populations at once with that probability, as the patch extinctions of Leibold et al. (2019); the site is recolonised by dispersal.

During colonisation, Poisson(seed_mean) individuals of every species are added to every site at each of the seed_steps. After the last of these, species absent from all sites can never return and are no longer computed.

Distributions from elsewhere, such as ranges, biogeographic reconstructions or the output of gen3sis, enter as pool and initial. With pool, a species can only occur where its value is TRUE (or 1): seeds go only there, and individuals that disperse to other sites are lost, as in a hostile matrix. A species without any site in pool dies out. initial replaces the first draw of Poisson(seed_mean) individuals with given abundances, or with one individual where a matrix of presences has 1; seeding still follows seed_steps, so use seed_steps = numeric(0) to start from initial alone. Both take one row per site and one column per species, named by species. Rows are matched by name when they have names (site1, site2 and so on in simulate_metacommunity()) and by position otherwise. Without them, results with the same seed are the same as before they existed. A tree from elsewhere, such as one simulated with gen3sis or a model of state-dependent diversification, enters through species_traits(); drop extinct lineages first, since they have no distribution.

Colonisation history

The simulation records, for every population (a species at a site) present at the last step, when and how it was founded, for arrival-dependent trait deviations in sample_individuals() (founder effects and monopolization):

  • arrival, the step at which the population was last founded: the first step at whose end it is present after being absent at the end of the previous one. Populations present at the end of step 1, from initial or the first draw of seeds, have arrival 1; a population lost to extirpation or competition and founded again gets the step of the new arrival.

  • propagule, the number of founders: the seeds (or initial individuals) and immigrants that reached the site at the step of arrival.

  • immigrants, the number of immigrants and seeds that reached the population after its arrival.

  • migrant_load, the sum over the steps since arrival of the share of the population made up of newcomers: immigrants over the abundance after dispersal, plus seeds over the abundance before reproduction. Each newcomer carries the species mean, so under complete mixing a deviation of the population shrinks by a factor \(1 - m_t \approx e^{-m_t}\) at a step where newcomers make up a share \(m_t\), and by about \(e^{-L}\) over the steps with migrant load \(L\).

Each is a sites x species matrix, NA for populations absent at the last step. Recording them takes no random draws, so abundances are the same as without them for the same seed. colonisation_history() returns them as a table.

Article and archived code

The article of Thompson et al. (2020) and the code archived with it (doi:10.5281/zenodo.3708350 ) differ in points that change results. Beta is gamma / alpha in the code and in their figures, but gamma - alpha in their Table 1. Their environment is converted to ranks, so it is uniform between 0 and 1, and the lowest dispersal is 0.00001, not 0.0001. Emigrants are Poisson in the code and binomial in the article, which comdynamite follows. In their competition-colonisation scenario, the code also halves the immigrants. See the article "Validating the model of Thompson et al. (2020)" on the package website for the complete list.

References

Thompson, P. L., Guzman, L. M., De Meester, L., Horváth, Z., Ptacnik, R., Vanschoenwinkel, B., Viana, D. S., & Chase, J. M. (2020). A process-based metacommunity framework linking local and regional scale community ecology. Ecology Letters, 23, 1314–1329. doi:10.1111/ele.13568

Leibold, M. A., Urban, M. C., De Meester, L., Klausmeier, C. A., & Vanoverbeke, J. (2019). Regional neutrality evolves through local adaptive niche evolution. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 116, 2612–2617. doi:10.1073/pnas.1808615116

Examples

set.seed(1)
ls <- landscape_implicit(30)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(20)
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(ls, species_traits(tr),
                              competition_matrix(tr, "phylo"),
                              dispersal = 0.01, n_steps = 200)
sim
#> <mc_sim> 30 sites x 20 species
#> species persisting: 18 of 20 
#> mean local richness: 7.03 
# a niche with two environmental axes
ls2 <- landscape_implicit(30)
niche2 <- species_traits(tr, rmax_range = c(1, 1))
sim2 <- simulate_metacommunity(ls, list(species_traits(tr), niche2),
                               competition_matrix(tr, "phylo"), n_steps = 200,
                               env = cbind(ls$env, ls2$env))
